accessibilityDefinitions.accessible-name: The interactive or informative surface has a stable discoverable name.
accessibilityDefinitions.actionable-role: The renderer exposes an action role with an activation mechanism.
accessibilityDefinitions.input-role: The renderer exposes the appropriate text, numeric, or value-entry role.
accessibilityDefinitions.value-state: The current value and its relevant state remain programmatically available.
accessibilityDefinitions.disabled-state: Disabled behavior is exposed without relying on color alone.
accessibilityDefinitions.loading-state: Pending work is represented and duplicate activation is prevented when applicable.
accessibilityDefinitions.invalid-state: Invalid state is exposed with an associated explanation.
accessibilityDefinitions.error-association: An error or validation message is associated with the affected control or record.
accessibilityDefinitions.selection-state: Committed selection is exposed independently from visual emphasis.
accessibilityDefinitions.expanded-state: Expanded or collapsed state is exposed with the controlled surface relationship.
accessibilityDefinitions.selected-state: Current navigation or collection selection is exposed programmatically.
accessibilityDefinitions.navigation-role: The navigation intent is exposed as a labelled destination or navigation region.
accessibilityDefinitions.labelled-surface: A contextual surface has an accessible title or label.
accessibilityDefinitions.focus-containment: Focus or the native accessibility cursor remains within an active task surface.
accessibilityDefinitions.focus-return: Dismissal returns focus or task context to the invoking control when applicable.
accessibilityDefinitions.dismissal: The surface has a discoverable dismissal path appropriate to the platform.
accessibilityDefinitions.focus-or-press-feedback: Keyboard focus or native press feedback remains visible and meaningful.
accessibilityDefinitions.keyboard-navigation: Keyboard or equivalent platform navigation reaches and operates the contract.
accessibilityDefinitions.ordered-structure: Order, grouping, and item relationships are available to assistive technology.
accessibilityDefinitions.structure-order: The structural reading and focus order follows the semantic composition.
accessibilityDefinitions.empty-state: An empty collection is communicated as content, not merely missing decoration.
accessibilityDefinitions.status-announcement: Meaningful status changes are announced through the renderer's live/status mechanism.
accessibilityDefinitions.non-color-status: Status meaning is available through text, structure, or an equivalent non-color cue.
accessibilityDefinitions.table-context: Rows, columns, headers, and comparable values retain usable context.
accessibilityDefinitions.sort-state: The current sort direction and sorted field are exposed programmatically.
accessibilityDefinitions.separator-role: A movable divider exposes its separator meaning and current value.
accessibilityDefinitions.keyboard-resize: A resizable divider has a keyboard or equivalent non-pointer adjustment path.
accessibilityDefinitions.supplemental-description: Supplemental help is associated with its trigger without becoming the only name.
accessibilityDefinitions.non-hover-alternative: Information revealed by hover has a focus, press, or explicit alternative.
accessibilityDefinitions.alternative-text: Non-text content has an appropriate alternative or is explicitly decorative.
accessibilityDefinitions.data-summary: A visualization has a meaningful textual summary or data access path.
accessibilityDefinitions.file-state: Selected, processing, complete, and failed file states are available as text/state.
accessibilityDefinitions.safe-area-inset: Content respects the platform safe-area boundary supplied by the renderer.
accessibilityDefinitions.virtual-keyboard: The layout and focus contract remains usable when the virtual keyboard is visible.
accessibilityDefinitions.hardware-capability: Hardware-dependent behavior exposes capability and failure states without assuming access.

web.notes: Trigger to popup/listbox or bounded list while preserving one selection intent.

native.notes: Trigger to sheet, native picker, or bounded list surface according to platform convention.

web.notes: Centered modal/dialog with a labelled task surface and focus containment.

native.notes: Native modal or sheet chosen by task intent; not every dialog is forced into a sheet.

web.notes: Edge contextual surface retaining parent route context and owned scroll.

native.notes: Sheet, modal, or navigation surface selected according to the contextual role.

web.notes: Persistent or collapsible information navigation in the application shell.

native.notes: Drawer, tabs, or stack navigation according to the product information architecture.

web.notes: Bounded primary destinations may render as a static or fixed mobile navigation slot; this is not a desktop sidebar or rail.

native.notes: Native tab/navigation treatment preserves a small destination set, active state, touch targets, and renderer-resolved safe-area insets.

web.notes: Bounded actions or choices use one trigger-owned popup with keyboard navigation and focus return.

native.notes: Native menus may use a platform menu or action sheet while preserving item intent, selection, and dismissal semantics.

web.notes: Anchored interactive content uses viewport collision handling, scoped focus behavior, and outside/Escape dismissal.

native.notes: Native renderers may present the same contextual content as a sheet or modal without inventing hover-only behavior.

web.notes: Dense table or grid interaction with explicit row, column, sort, and selection meaning.

native.notes: Usually list/detail, cards/rows, or intentionally horizontally scrollable data when comparison justifies it.

web.notes: Readable tabular comparison keeps native table semantics without query, selection, or cell-editing behavior.

native.notes: Native renderers may present the same bounded comparison as a readable record list or detail surface.

web.notes: Simultaneous list and detail panes when the bounded surface supports them.

native.notes: List to detail navigation or a sheet/detail stack without changing record intent.

web.notes: Calendar, popup, or bounded list controls with text entry where the contract supports it.

native.notes: Platform date/time controls when they improve entry and preserve the shared value contract.

web.notes: File input, dropzone, or drag/drop selection without owning storage or transport.

native.notes: Document picker, photo library, camera, or share/import affordance according to capability.

web.notes: Keyboard-first search and execution of a bounded command set.

native.notes: Search/action surface reachable from the native shell without assuming browser shortcuts.

web.notes: Keep one primary action direct while exposing tightly related alternatives through the canonical overlay trigger.

native.notes: Keep the primary press direct and present alternatives in a platform menu or sheet without changing the action intent.

web.notes: A bounded notification collection may render as a popover, drawer, or dedicated page surface according to shell context.

native.notes: Native notification history uses a sheet or screen while preserving read, clear, and action semantics.

web.notes: Shell navigation and context follow the responsive Web shell contract.

native.notes: Native shell presentation owns safe areas, stacks, tabs, and platform back behavior.

web.notes: Keep primary query controls near the collection and expose applied state.

native.notes: Move secondary filtering into a sheet while keeping search and the filter trigger reachable.

web.notes: Use the collection's declared comparison and selection semantics.

native.notes: Use rows, cards, or incremental loading without requiring table markup.

web.notes: Bounded scroll rail with keyboard and indicator controls.

native.notes: Swipe/gesture surface with explicit controls and preserved slide order.

web.notes: Tree semantics preserve level, position, expansion, and selection context.

native.notes: Nested list or list/detail presentation preserves hierarchy and selection meaning.

web.notes: Content-first product and cart composition uses shared primitives and commerce contracts.

native.notes: Native list/card/cart presentation keeps product meaning and bounded quantity actions.

safeArea.note: The native renderer supplies insets; the product decides which shell/content regions consume them.

virtualKeyboard.note: The renderer adapts visible content and focus while the consumer owns submission and validation.

camera.note: Capability and permission failures are presented semantically; capture policy remains consumer-owned.

qrScanner.note: Scanning is a native capability boundary; Ten4Seven may present scanner states without resolving the decoded business meaning.

photoLibrary.note: The native picker supplies selected media; the consumer owns storage and upload behavior.

documentPicker.note: The native picker supplies a file selection; the consumer owns transport and lifecycle.

haptics.note: Haptic intent is an optional renderer affordance and never replaces visual or accessible feedback.

pushEntry.note: Push entry can select a presentation surface; the application resolves destination and authorization.

deepLink.note: The application resolves links and guards; the system supplies the destination presentation pattern.

offline.note: Connectivity truth is consumer/platform-owned; Ten4Seven owns reusable presentation vocabulary.

sync.note: The sync engine, cursor, conflict policy, and retry truth remain outside component contracts.

networkRetry.note: Retry availability may be presented, but retry policy and idempotency remain consumer-owned.

secureStorage.note: Secure storage is a platform capability; token and component contracts never persist credentials.

backgroundTask.note: Background scheduling and task guarantees remain application/platform policy.

permissions.note: The system presents permission or unavailable states; it never decides entitlement or access truth.
